artifacts.summary: Recommends flock on the existing guard's own documented .lake/build-guard.lock path (no coupling to .claude/) to fix the C1 build race, and creating scripts/nolints-style.txt while reconciling a now-contradicted ci.yml comment for the second item.

memory_candidates.content: lake-build-guard.sh's serialization lock lives at a documented, stable convention path: <project-root>/.lake/build-guard.lock (resolved by walking up to the nearest lakefile.toml/lakefile.lean). Any other script needing to serialize its own `lake build` calls against the guard can simply flock that same path directly -- no need to invoke the guard binary, probe for .claude/, or modify the guard at all, since flock() mutual exclusion is cooperative per-path, not per-binary. This also means the fix works identically in a checkout with no agent system deployed (the lock still serializes the script's own builds against itself, harmlessly).

Mathlib's vendored lint-style.lean (.lake/packages/mathlib/scripts/lint-style.lean) unconditionally tries to read scripts/nolints-style.txt relative to cwd and prints a warning when absent, unrelated to this repo's own scripts/nolints.json (a different file, used by check-module-invariants.sh's C16/env_linter baseline). A repo cannot silence the vendored tool's warning by any means other than creating the file; lines starting with '--' in that file are treated as comments and ignored, so a file containing only a header comment is a valid, zero-exception nolints-style.txt.
